hints: Notice the question asks for maximum frequency, which occurs at the instant the $25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ buzzer velocity points directly toward the stationary observer.
Connect this to the moving-source Doppler effect: approaching compresses the $340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ sound waves so observed wavelength is shortened and observed frequency is raised.
Set up $f_o = f_s v/(v-v_s)$ with $f_s = 846\text{ Hz}$, $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v_s = 25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, then evaluate the denominator $340-25.0$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: source frequency $f_s = 846\text{ Hz}$, source speed $v_s = 25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, wave speed $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, observer stationary.
State the rule: for a source moving toward a stationary observer the observed frequency is increased to $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ because successive wavefronts are emitted closer together.
Set up the maximum-frequency case: use the minus sign because the component of buzzer velocity toward the observer is the full $25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at closest approach.
Calculate: $340/315 \approx 1.0794$, so $f_o \approx 846 \times 1.0794 \approx 913\text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as required.

options.A: Too low to be the approaching-source frequency. It is below even the receding minimum of about $788\text{ Hz}$.
options.B: This is the minimum frequency when the $25.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ buzzer moves directly away, using $340+25.0$ in the denominator.
options.C: This is the moving-observer result $846 \times (340+25.0)/340$. Here the source moves, so divide by $340-25.0$, not multiply.
options.D: Approaching source gives $846 \times 340/(340-25.0) \approx 913\text{ Hz}$, the largest observed frequency.
